c.tagline: Eight million stories on one electric grid.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets and hustler scams (costumed characters, CD pushers) around Times Square, and stay alert on empty late-night subway platforms.

hood_desc: The bustling commercial core of Times Square, Broadway theaters, skyscrapers, and major hotels, ideal for first-time visitors, theatergoers, and business travelers.
A chic downtown district of cast-iron architecture, cobblestone streets, designer boutiques, and art galleries, perfect for luxury shoppers and style-conscious travelers.
A charming, tree-lined bohemian neighborhood of brownstones, jazz clubs, cozy cafes, and NYU energy, appealing to romantics, students, and those seeking a laid-back vibe.
A hip Brooklyn hotspot of indie boutiques, waterfront views, craft breweries, and a thriving art and music scene, great for trendsetters and nightlife lovers.
An affluent, refined district of elegant townhouses, Museum Mile, and upscale Madison Avenue shopping, suiting culture lovers, families, and luxury travelers.
lodging: The New Yorker A Wyndham Hotel

water.note: Tap water is treated and safe to drink throughout the city.

transit.pay: The MetroCard is gone — payment is now OMNY: just tap a contactless bank card or phone at the turnstile. No bank card? Buy an OMNY card for $1 at station vending machines and many shops. A ride costs $3.00, and after 12 paid taps in a week the rest are free; the Staten Island Ferry is free.
transit.hours: The subway runs 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, though late-night service is less frequent.
